evidence.reference_title: Oligophrenin 1 (OPHN1) gene mutation causes syndromic X-linked mental retardation with epilepsy, rostral ventricular enlargement and cerebellar hypoplasia.
evidence.snippet: Neuroimaging displayed fronto-temporal atrophy with rostral enlargement of the lateral ventricles, lower vermian agenesis and asymmetric cerebellar hypoplasia.

evidence.reference_title: Comprehensive Structural MRI Phenotyping in Oligophrenin 1-Related Disorder Reveals Characteristic Brain Malformations.
evidence.snippet: We identified a consistent constellation of structural abnormalities, including cerebellar vermian and hemispheric hypoplasia with dysfoliation, brainstem malformations including aberrant tracts such as anterior mesencephalic cap dysplasia, and abnormal transverse pontine fibers; and supratentorial features such as caudate hypoplasia, frontal-predominant ventriculomegaly, and commissural anomalies.

nodes.description: Hypoplasia and dysgenesis of the vermis, with incomplete sulcation that is most marked in lobules VI and VII. It is the radiological hallmark, but a minority of molecularly confirmed males have no cerebellar anomaly on MRI.

evidence.reference_title: Delineation of the clinical phenotype associated with OPHN1 mutations based on the clinical and neuropsychological evaluation of three families.
evidence.snippet: Our study confirms that cerebellar hypoplasia is a hallmark of this syndrome.

evidence.reference_title: Novel intragenic deletion in OPHN1 in a family causing XLMR with cerebellar hypoplasia and distinctive facial appearance.
evidence.snippet: The boys had moderate MR, seizure disorder, facial dysmorphism, and cerebellar vermis hypoplasia.

evidence.reference_title: A novel in-frame deletion affecting the BAR domain of OPHN1 in a family with intellectual disability and hippocampal alterations.
evidence.snippet: Cranial MRI scans showed large lateral ventricles, vermis hypoplasia and cystic dilatation of the cisterna magna in all affected males.

evidence.reference_title: Expanding the phenotypic spectrum associated with OPHN1 mutations: Report of 17 individuals with intellectual disability but no cerebellar hypoplasia.
evidence.snippet: Here we report on 17 individuals from four unrelated families affected by mild to severe intellectual disability due to OPHN1 mutations without cerebellar anomaly on brain MRI.

nodes.description: The cerebellar malformation is the clinical hallmark but its mechanism is the least understood part of the disease. Patients show incomplete sulcation of the anterior and posterior vermis, worst in lobules VI and VII, with vermian and hemispheric hypoplasia and dysfoliation; a female fetus with a partial OPHN1 deletion and skewed X inactivation had Purkinje cell heterotopia in the cerebellar white matter. Detailed MRI also shows aberrant brainstem tracts, which the authors read as a defect of axon guidance and cerebrocerebellar connectivity. The Ophn1 knockout mouse has a normal cerebellum, so no model reproduces this step.

animal_models.description: The cerebellum of the knockout is morphologically normal.

evidence.reference_title: Specific clinical and brain MRI features in mentally retarded patients with mutations in the Oligophrenin-1 gene.
evidence.snippet: Brain MRIs performed in three individuals exhibited a specific vermian dysgenesis including an incomplete sulcation of anterior and posterior vermis with the most prominent defect in lobules VI and VII.

evidence.reference_title: Neuropathological features in a female fetus with OPHN1 deletion and cerebellar hypoplasia.
evidence.snippet: Neuropathological examination of the female fetus revealed cerebellar hypoplasia and the heterotopia of Purkinje cells at multiple sites in the white matter of the cerebellum.

evidence.reference_title: Comprehensive Structural MRI Phenotyping in Oligophrenin 1-Related Disorder Reveals Characteristic Brain Malformations.
evidence.snippet: The combination of gray and white matter involvement, together with DTI evidence of aberrant fibers, supports a pathogenic mechanism involving abnormal regional development, disrupted cerebrocerebellar connectivity, and impaired axonal guidance.

evidence.reference_title: Loss of X-linked mental retardation gene oligophrenin1 in mice impairs spatial memory and leads to ventricular enlargement and dendritic spine immaturity.
evidence.snippet: We generated a mouse model of ophn1 deficiency and showed that it mimics the ventricles enlargement without affecting the cerebellum morphoanatomy.

nodes.description: Reduced oligophrenin-1 shortens dendritic spines in hippocampal CA1 neurons, and Ophn1 knockout neurons carry fewer mature spines and more immature protrusions, with reduced dendritic complexity in dentate granule cells. Synapse density is normal. Spine defects are not reversed by acute kinase inhibition, unlike the functional synaptic defects.

evidence.reference_title: The X-linked mental retardation protein oligophrenin-1 is required for dendritic spine morphogenesis.
evidence.snippet: Using RNA interference and antisense RNA approaches, we show that knock-down of oligophrenin-1 levels in CA1 neurons in rat hippocampal slices significantly decreases spine length.

evidence.reference_title: Loss of X-linked mental retardation gene oligophrenin1 in mice impairs spatial memory and leads to ventricular enlargement and dendritic spine immaturity.
evidence.snippet: This altered short-term plasticity that reflects changes in the release of neurotransmitters from the presynaptic processes is associated with normal synaptic density together with a reduction in mature dendritic spines.

evidence.reference_title: Rapid reversal of impaired inhibitory and excitatory transmission but not spine dysgenesis in a mouse model of mental retardation.
evidence.snippet: Lack of oligophrenin-1 resulted in reductions in dendritic tree complexity and mature dendritic spine density and in evoked and spontaneous EPSCs and IPSCs.

evidence.snippet: Mutation analysis of the OPHN1 gene on Xq12 disclosed a genomic deletion of exon 19 causing a frameshift.

nodes.description: Hyperactivity and low frustration tolerance are frequent; the Ophn1 knockout mouse is also hyperactive.

evidence.reference_title: A novel in-frame deletion affecting the BAR domain of OPHN1 in a family with intellectual disability and hippocampal alterations.
evidence.snippet: Features shared by the affected males of this family include neonatal hypotonia, strabismus, prominent root of the nose, deep set eyes, hyperactivity and instability/intolerance to frustration.

evidence.reference_title: OPHN1-related neurodevelopmental disorders: clinical and genetic findings with novel variants.
evidence.snippet: Neuropsychiatric features, including autism spectrum disorder and hyperactivity, were also observed, highlighting phenotypic variability.

evidence.reference_title: Loss of X-linked mental retardation gene oligophrenin1 in mice impairs spatial memory and leads to ventricular enlargement and dendritic spine immaturity.
evidence.snippet: The ophn1 knock-out mice exhibit behavioral defects in spatial memory together with impairment in social behavior, lateralization, and hyperactivity.

nodes.description: Activity drives oligophrenin-1 into dendritic spines, where it stabilizes synaptic AMPA receptors; without it glutamatergic synapses fail to mature. Ophn1 knockout mice show reduced paired-pulse facilitation, near-complete loss of hippocampal long-term depression, and loss of PKA-dependent presynaptic plasticity, while CA1 long-term potentiation is normal. Rapid dendritic synthesis of OPHN1 after group I mGluR activation is needed for mGluR-dependent long-term depression. The knockout also has fewer adult-born dentate granule neurons.

evidence.reference_title: The Rho-linked mental retardation protein oligophrenin-1 controls synapse maturation and plasticity by stabilizing AMPA receptors.
evidence.snippet: Synaptic activity through NMDA receptor activation drives OPHN1 into dendritic spines, where it forms a complex with AMPA receptors, and selectively enhances AMPA-receptor-mediated synaptic transmission and spine size by stabilizing synaptic AMPA receptors.

evidence.reference_title: The Rho-linked mental retardation protein oligophrenin-1 controls synapse maturation and plasticity by stabilizing AMPA receptors.
evidence.snippet: Consequently, decreased or defective OPHN1 signaling prevents glutamatergic synapse maturation and causes loss of synaptic structure, function, and plasticity.

evidence.reference_title: Pharmacological rescue of adult hippocampal neurogenesis in a mouse model of X-linked intellectual disability.
evidence.snippet: We found that mice lacking Ophn1 display a reduction in the number of newborn neurons in the dentate gyrus.

evidence.reference_title: Rapid synthesis of the X-linked mental retardation protein OPHN1 mediates mGluR-dependent LTD through interaction with the endocytic machinery.
evidence.snippet: This response is essential for mGluR-LTD, as acute blockade of OPHN1 synthesis impedes LTD.

nodes.description: Through its BAR domain and SH3-binding partners, including endophilin A1, oligophrenin-1 is recruited to endocytic sites, where it keeps ROCK from inhibiting clathrin-mediated endocytosis. Loss of Ophn1 slows synaptic vesicle retrieval at the presynaptic terminal and reduces postsynaptic AMPA receptor internalization. At the postsynaptic side, binding to Homer1b/c positions the spine endocytic zone next to the postsynaptic density, which local AMPA receptor recycling requires.

evidence.reference_title: The Rho-linked mental retardation protein OPHN1 controls synaptic vesicle endocytosis via endophilin A1.
evidence.snippet: We further demonstrate that OPHN1 forms a complex with endophilin A1, a protein implicated in membrane curvature generation during SV endocytosis and, importantly, that OPHN1's interaction with endophilin A1 and its Rho-GAP activity are important for its function in SV endocytosis.

evidence.reference_title: The Rho-linked mental retardation protein OPHN1 controls synaptic vesicle endocytosis via endophilin A1.
evidence.snippet: In particular, we show that OPHN1 knockdown affects the kinetic efficiency of endocytosis.

evidence.reference_title: The X-linked mental retardation protein OPHN1 interacts with Homer1b/c to control spine endocytic zone positioning and expression of synaptic potentiation.
evidence.snippet: Disruption of the OPHN1-Homer1b/c interaction causes a displacement of EZs from the PSD, along with impaired AMPAR recycling and reduced AMPAR accumulation at synapses, in both basal conditions and conditions that can induce synaptic potentiation.

nodes.description: Ophn1 knockout mice have reduced inhibitory transmission from a smaller readily releasable pool and slower vesicle recycling at inhibitory synapses, altered parvalbumin, somatostatin and neuropeptide Y interneuron populations, and hippocampal epileptiform activity. Seven weeks of fasudil in adult mice corrected the electrographic and interneuron changes, while acute dosing did not. Loss of Ophn1 in prefrontal parvalbumin interneurons alone is enough to cause stress-induced helpless behaviour in mice.

evidence.reference_title: ROCK/PKA Inhibition Rescues Hippocampal Hyperexcitability and GABAergic Neuron Alterations in a Oligophrenin-1 Knock-Out Mouse Model of X-Linked Intellectual Disability.
evidence.snippet: While acute administration of fasudil had no impact on seizure activity, seven weeks of treatment in adulthood were able to correct electrographic, neuroanatomical and synaptic alterations of Ophn1 deficient mice.

evidence.reference_title: Oligophrenin-1 moderates behavioral responses to stress by regulating parvalbumin interneuron activity in the medial prefrontal cortex.
evidence.snippet: Strikingly, Ophn1 deletion exclusively in parvalbumin (PV) interneurons in the prelimbic medial prefrontal cortex (PL-mPFC) is sufficient to induce helplessness.

nodes.description: Moderate to severe in most affected males; mild in some families and in symptomatic carrier females. Severity varies within families.

evidence.snippet: The distinctive phenotype comprised moderate to severe mental retardation, myoclonic-astatic epilepsy, ataxia, strabismus and hypogenitalism.

evidence.snippet: Our findings, however, indicate that OPHN1 mutations result in a recognizable syndrome.

evidence.reference_title: Expanding the phenotypic spectrum associated with OPHN1 mutations: Report of 17 individuals with intellectual disability but no cerebellar hypoplasia.
evidence.snippet: Among the identified OPHN1 mutations, we report for the first time a missense mutation occurring in a mosaic state.

nodes.description: Reported alleles are nonsense, frameshift, splice-site and exon-level deletions, most of them in the region encoding the central RhoGAP domain and predicted to abolish the protein. In-frame changes in the N-terminal BAR domain (a 16-amino-acid insertion; loss of exon 7) give the same clinical picture, so they are read as loss of function too. Oligophrenin-1 is a RhoGAP: it accelerates GTP hydrolysis by RhoA and so switches the pathway off. It also binds F-actin, Homer and the endocytic protein endophilin A1.

evidence.reference_title: Oligophrenin-1 encodes a rhoGAP protein involved in X-linked mental retardation.
evidence.snippet: Here we report the characterization of a new gene on the long arm of the X-chromosome (position Xq12) and the identification in unrelated individuals of different mutations that are predicted to cause a loss of function.

evidence.reference_title: Oligophrenin-1 encodes a rhoGAP protein involved in X-linked mental retardation.
evidence.snippet: This gene is highly expressed in fetal brain and encodes a protein of relative molecular mass 91K, named oligophrenin-1, which contains a domain typical of a Rho-GTPase-activating protein (rhoGAP).

evidence.reference_title: Novel unconventional variants expand the allelic spectrum of OPHN1 gene.
evidence.snippet: In most of cases so far reported, the identified genomic variants involve the region encoding the central RhoGAP domain of the oligophrenin-1 protein, and are predicted to result in a complete loss of function.

evidence.reference_title: Insertion of 16 amino acids in the BAR domain of the oligophrenin 1 protein causes mental retardation and cerebellar hypoplasia in an Italian family.
evidence.snippet: In fact, the clinical phenotype of these patients is identical to that of patients with loss-of-function mutations.

evidence.reference_title: OPHN1 / X-linked intellectual disability-cerebellar hypoplasia syndrome (Definitive)
evidence.snippet: The mechanism of pathogenicity is reported to be loss of function.

evidence.reference_title: The RhoGAP activity of OPHN1, a new F-actin-binding protein, is negatively controlled by its amino-terminal domain.
evidence.snippet: Overexpression experiments in fibroblasts showed that the OPHN1 RhoGAP domain regulates in vivo the actin cytoskeleton by inhibition of Rho pathways.

nodes.description: Human induced pluripotent stem cells lacking OPHN1 function, differentiated towards neurons. ROCK activity normally falls as neurons differentiate but stays high in OPHN1-deficient cells, and the ROCK inhibitor fasudil restores neuronal morphology and upregulates the neurite-outgrowth nuclear receptor NR4A1.

Hemizygous null males have enlarged lateral ventricles, spatial memory and social deficits, hyperactivity, immature dendritic spines, reduced synaptic vesicle and AMPA receptor endocytosis with loss of hippocampal long-term depression, cAMP/PKA dysregulation and hippocampal epileptiform activity, but a normal cerebellum. Many of these phenotypes are reversed by the ROCK/PKA inhibitor fasudil, including in adults.

Ophn1 knockout mice show brain-region-specific dysregulation of cAMP/PKA signalling, with loss of PKA-dependent presynaptic plasticity in hippocampus and amygdala, and PKA overactivity in the medial prefrontal cortex that impairs spatial working memory. The INCREASED direction comes from the medial prefrontal cortex result, where PKA overactivity underlies the working-memory deficit; in hippocampus and amygdala the reported change is a loss of PKA-dependent presynaptic plasticity, so the direction is region-specific. How loss of a RhoGAP reaches PKA is not established.

evidence.reference_title: Lack of the presynaptic RhoGAP protein oligophrenin1 leads to cognitive disabilities through dysregulation of the cAMP/PKA signalling pathway.
evidence.snippet: At the behavioural level, lack of OPHN1 resulted in hippocampus- and amygdala-related learning disabilities which could be fully rescued by the ROCK/PKA kinase inhibitor fasudil.

nodes.description: Early-onset epilepsy is common; reported seizure types include complex partial (focal impaired awareness) seizures and myoclonic-astatic epilepsy, with variable severity within families.

evidence.reference_title: Specific clinical and brain MRI features in mentally retarded patients with mutations in the Oligophrenin-1 gene.
evidence.snippet: Clinical data shared by affected individuals were neonatal hypotonia with motor delay but no obvious ataxia, marked strabismus, early onset complex partial seizures, and moderate to severe MR.

evidence.reference_title: Oligophrenin 1 (OPHN1) gene mutation causes syndromic X-linked mental retardation with epilepsy, rostral ventricular enlargement and cerebellar hypoplasia.
evidence.snippet: The distinctive phenotype comprised moderate to severe mental retardation, myoclonic-astatic epilepsy, ataxia, strabismus and hypogenitalism.

evidence.reference_title: Novel intragenic deletion in OPHN1 in a family causing XLMR with cerebellar hypoplasia and distinctive facial appearance.
evidence.snippet: The boys had moderate MR, seizure disorder, facial dysmorphism, and cerebellar vermis hypoplasia.

nodes.description: Without oligophrenin-1, RhoA stays in its active GTP-bound state and its effector Rho-kinase (ROCK) is overactive in neurons and astrocytes. Most downstream cellular phenotypes of Ophn1 deficiency are reproduced by activated RhoA and reversed by ROCK inhibitors, which is the basis for the fasudil studies in the knockout mouse. Fasudil also inhibits PKA, so rescue by fasudil does not by itself separate the two kinases.

evidence.reference_title: Inhibition of RhoA pathway rescues the endocytosis defects in Oligophrenin1 mouse model of mental retardation.
evidence.snippet: Through interactions with Src homology 3 domain containing proteins involved in CME, OPHN1 is concentrated to endocytic sites where it down-regulates the RhoA/ROCK signaling pathway and represses the inhibitory function of ROCK on endocytosis.

evidence.reference_title: Protein Kinase A Deregulation in the Medial Prefrontal Cortex Impairs Working Memory in Murine Oligophrenin-1 Deficiency.
evidence.snippet: Upregulation of both PKA and ROCK has been reported in Ophn1-/y mice, but it remains unclear whether kinase hyperactivity contributes to the behavioral phenotypes.

evidence.reference_title: Rho Kinase Inhibition Is Essential During In Vitro Neurogenesis and Promotes Phenotypic Rescue of Human Induced Pluripotent Stem Cell-Derived Neurons With Oligophrenin-1 Loss of Function.
evidence.snippet: We show that during in vitro neurogenesis, ROCK activity decreases from day 10 until terminal differentiation, whereas in OPHN1-deficient human induced pluripotent stem cells (h-iPSCs), the levels of ROCK are elevated throughout differentiation.
